key_insight: PIML-OFEM combines overlapping finite elements with problem-independent machine learning to reuse local basis functions across load cases and boundary conditions for large-scale heterogeneous structures.
engineering_relevance: It enables faster, high-resolution structural analysis and topology optimization while preserving accuracy for complex material distributions.
method: Retain only corner-node DOFs for each substructure.
Build oversampled basis functions on extended domains and restrict them to the target substructure.
Use a U-Net to predict local basis functions from Young's modulus maps and blend them with partition-of-unity overlap.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with fine-scale FEM in displacement and elemental strain energy, with lower online cost than direct FEM and better accuracy than linear-interpolation PIML substructure models.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and generalization of the learned basis predictions, especially for unseen material patterns or highly irregular heterogeneity.
paper_title: PIML-OFEM: A New Large-Scale Structural Analysis Method Based on Problem-Independent Machine Learning and Overlapping Finite Element Technique
